ambiguities: PRB-013: WEB-6 says the focus stop comes after the Select all of its column, but it does not say which Tab stop follows the focus stop; I took the next column's Select all.

PRB-017, PRB-026: DAT-8 says a card goes to its old position number, or to the end if the column is shorter. When the position equals the current length, the text does not say whether it is inserted there or appended; I inserted it at that position.
PRB-023: CRY-3 counts cards whose middle is above the pointer. The text does not say what happens when the pointer is exactly at a middle; I did not count the card whose middle the pointer is on.
PRB-004: the rules give no focus target when the 'Try again' button leaves the page; I used FOC-1 and took the place title.
PRB-022: the 'full' check in DAT-7 counts cards still marked 'Saving…'; I counted them.
NAV-T1 row 1 says focus is not moved on a reload, while MEM-T1 keeps a focus stop that is 'first visible' on reload. The text does not say whether the focus stop has focus after a reload.
contradictions: FCS-2 and CRY-2 both say 'the nearest column on that side' but differ. FCS-2 requires a column with a visible card, so from In progress it skips the empty Review and goes to Done. CRY-2 requires a loaded column, and Empty counts as loaded, so it goes to Review. (PRB-011 uses FCS-2; PRB-021 uses CRY-2.)

MIS-1 says that while Missing.Page shows, Slate keeps the address as the user entered it. NAV-1 says that when Slate shows an address, it rewrites the current entry to the written form. For an unknown address such as #/nowhere, the written form is not defined, so the two rules disagree on what the address becomes.
